answer: A thousand keys can be minted, but a ferrous fingerprint cannot: the oscillator decay inside each signing device leaves a measurable timing skew. I would score identity by the reef of co-signers around that skew. Honest operators sit on unrelated hardware, so their skews scatter across the graph. A clone farm signs from one machine, and one machine repeats the same skew across ocean-wide histories no matter how many addresses it wears. The cost of faking becomes buying and aging a separate clock per identity, which prices sybils at hardware rates instead of key rates.
